verdict: This is the most clinically literate consumer weight app I have audited: the protein architecture (1.6 g/kg GLP-1-current / 1.2 default, clamped, one formula), the >1%/wk rapid-loss tripwire that responds with "eat enough, protect muscle" instead of applause, the SCOFF gate with a GLP-1-adjusted core count, and trend-over-scale with luteal water-weight pre-framing are all things I say in clinic and almost never see in an app. The gaps are cohort-shaped, not philosophy-shaped: the on-medication chapter is blind to the weekly injection rhythm that dominates its users' lives (no dose-day context, no side-effect burden, no fluids care), and the post-medication cohort — the highest-regain-risk population in this market — gets a noun phrase and a protein note instead of the band-zone surveillance machinery the app already owns. Fix the two cohort gaps and this is quietly a care-delivery chassis, not just a coach persona.

keep.what: The protein architecture in /Users/bko/plankAI/PlankApp/Program/TargetsService.swift — ONE formula, 1.6 g/kg GLP-1-current with 90–140g clamp, 1.2 g/kg default with 70–130g clamp, 5g rounding ('guidance, not false precision'), WeeklyReview's consented ±10g applied BEFORE the advisory clamp
keep.why: Matches the multi-society advisory band for lean-mass preservation during incretin pharmacotherapy; the pre-clamp adjustment order means an eased floor can never exit the safe band. Most consumer apps still hand these women 0.8 g/kg or macro percentages.

keep.what: RapidLossTripwire + pace clamps: DailyBriefEngine.swift:157 renders '>1%/wk sustained' as 'you're losing faster than 1% a week. protein protects muscle', TargetsService.planImpliedRate clamps to ≤1%/wk even on corrupt plan data, CalorieTargetCalculator floors at max(1200, BMR)
keep.why: Treating fast loss as a muscle-risk event rather than a win is the exact inversion of the consumer-app norm and is standard of care for my GLP-1 patients; the BMR floor is stronger than the industry's flat-1200 habit.

keep.what: The safety gate in ProgramGoalCalculator.swift: SCOFF ≥2 routing with scoffCoreYesCount excluding the two GLP-1-expected items, BMI-18.5 goal-weight floor, pregnancy/breastfeeding/TTC pace caps, insulin/sulfonylurea → clinicianFirst terminal, ED numeric suppression threaded through TargetsService and chat
keep.why: The GLP-1-adjusted SCOFF core count prevents false-routing pharmacotherapy patients into the recovery arm (rapid loss + quieted food thoughts are drug effects, not ED signals) — a subtlety most clinical intake forms miss. The hypoglycemia screen is the one question that genuinely prevents harm.

keep.what: Trend-over-scale with honest floors: EMA trend gated on 3+ weigh-ins over 5+ days, 'your trend is up… usually water, not fat', and BodyLine.season naming luteal water retention BEFORE the scale moves (Signals.swift:721-729), with the juxtaposition-never-causation law
keep.why: Pre-framing cyclical water weight is the highest-yield piece of scale counseling I do in clinic; the 'alongside, never because' rule keeps correlational habit-trend pairings scientifically honest.

keep.what: The on-medication inversion: fast row hidden (TodayView.swift:536), fuel frame 'first plate at X · eating early protects your muscle', 'low appetite? eat on schedule, not on hunger' (WeekIntent rhythm_block), plateau pre-registered in ProgramArc (clock ~wk 9-13 + EMA-flat ≥3wks trigger), and chat redlines routing all dose/stop/switch questions to her clinician
keep.why: Mechanical eating on a schedule is verbatim what we teach anorexic-appetite GLP-1 patients; pre-registering the plateau in the program's structure ('the plan expects it') defuses the moment most patients quit.

problems.title: Post-GLP-1 cohort has no structural regain surveillance — the app's own best machinery is pointed away from them
problems.evidence: Chapter.derive in /Users/bko/plankAI/PlankApp/Program/DayModel.swift:32-36 — only glp1Status 'current' → .onMedication; 'past' falls to .losing/.keeping. Band drift/reset zones (DailyBriefEngine.swift:169-187) run ONLY in .keeping. Post-GLP-1 gets a protein note ('keeps the loss kept', TargetsService.swift:140) and a notification noun phrase.
problems.detail: Discontinuation regain is the defining physiology of this cohort (~two-thirds of lost weight regained within a year in the STEP-1 extension; rapid regain in SURMOUNT-4 withdrawal), and appetite returns with force in weeks 2–8 off drug. A 'past' user still losing sits in the losing chapter with no armed band, no appetite-return normalization (the moment she interprets returning food noise as personal failure), no tightened trend cadence, and no strength carry-over from the on-med chapter. The strategy doc names post-GLP-1 a primary cohort; the engine gives them the generic path.

problems.title: On-medication chapter is blind to the injection-week rhythm: no dose-day context, no side-effect burden, no fluids care
problems.evidence: grep across PlankApp/ and Packages/ finds zero occurrences of nausea/dose/injection/shot-day/hydration handling; docs/app_v6/00_RESEARCH.md §3 explicitly kills the hydration module ('no data stream'); the on-med week plan (WeekIntent.swift:108-123) is invariant across the injection week.
problems.detail: GI side effects cluster 1–2 days post-injection, drive under-fueling and protein misses, and are the #1 discontinuation driver I see. 'Eat on schedule, not on hunger' is right on a good day and wrong on a nausea day (small, bland, fluids-first is the counsel). The app that promises to 'notice patterns before she does' models her sleep and her cycle but not the single strongest weekly rhythm in an on-med user's life. One collected scheduling fact — which day is shot day — plus the plate exhaust it already holds (a <~800 kcal on-med day is detectable by evening) would let the day soften itself. Dehydration lines are a compliance-safe care gap: no logging needed, just dose-day-adjacent 'fluids first' framing.

problems.title: Sarcopenia attention collapses to a protein number: strength is rendered as optional garnish for the exact cohort that needs it as co-therapy
problems.evidence: DayModel.swift:288-294 (v6.4): '.workout, .breath: return true' — workouts always optional ('if you feel like it', screenshot 02) unless promoted to the one-thing; WeekIntent strength_block ('two short strength sessions protect muscle') names it one week in four, but the day list demotes it daily; no strength receipt exists in the signals band (TodaySignals.swift).
problems.detail: Protein alone does not preserve lean mass under incretin therapy — the advisory guidance pairs protein with resistance training as co-equal. For .onMedication, two short strength sessions/week is the other half of the prescription; presenting it under 'if you feel like it' communicates it is decorative. There is also no muscle-relevant functional signal anywhere (strength-session cadence, carrying/stairs NSVs), so 'muscle preservation' is one number plus one optional row.

problems.title: The v6.4 'overnight fast' checkable row drifts from observed-to-prescribed, against the app's own engine law
problems.evidence: TodayView.swift:441-482 + fastRowModel:535-553 — the fast is a required-section row with a check ring whose done-state is 'hours >= 12'; screenshot 01/02 shows 'overnight fast · starts with tonight's dinner' with an empty ring; window sheet (screenshot 08) titled 'WHY FASTING HELPS'; CoachSummary #3 (Signals.swift:805-813) coaches 'stop eating a little earlier… gets you near 12'. QuietHours.swift header states 'time-restricted-eating claims don't clear our evidence bar… never a target'.
problems.detail: The clamps genuinely hold (praise saturates at 14h, care at 16h+, GLP-1 chapter excluded at TodayView:536, restriction-risk/numeric-suppressed gated via QuietHours.mayNarrate), and a 12h overnight window is conservative advice. But a daily check ring that fills at ≥12h IS a target with a failable state — prescription grammar — in a demographic where fasting behavior is one of the strongest prospective predictors of binge-eating onset (the app's own cited research, PMC10589984). The founder override and the engine law now contradict each other in shipped UI. Flagging as founder-decision: keep the row, drop the ring/done-state (render as a measured receipt).

problems.title: Window-sheet science copy overstates single-study findings as settled fact
problems.evidence: Screenshot 08: 'keeping it near 12 to 14 hours trimmed intake and improved insulin sensitivity, and the same food eaten earlier stores less.' BecomingView.swift:370: 'a steady 12 to 14 hour overnight fast trims intake and stores less.'
problems.detail: 'The same food eaten earlier stores less' generalizes one crossover trial's adipose gene-expression finding (Vujović 2022, n=16) into a metabolic promise; TRE meta-analytic effects are modest (−1.3 to −1.9 kg vs control). The register should be 'in trials, people who… tended to' — the app does this well elsewhere (BodyLine's 'alongside'). As written it is the one surface a regulator or a physician reviewer would circle.

problems.title: Rapid-loss care is one generic line for all cohorts; no on-med variant and no clinician-visit bridge
problems.evidence: RapidLossTripwire.swift (careMessage: 'you're losing faster than we plan for. let's make sure you're eating enough') and DailyBriefEngine.swift:157-165 — same >1%/wk rule regardless of chapter; the chat redline routes medication questions out but the tripwire never suggests bringing the trend to her prescriber.
problems.detail: On semaglutide 2.4/tirzepatide, >1%/wk early loss is common; the correct consumer-safe response is exactly what ships (protein + fueling) PLUS 'this trend is worth showing your clinician at your next visit' — care navigation, not diagnosis, fully inside legal bounds. Post-GLP-1 has the mirror gap: no rapid-REGAIN tripwire outside the keeping chapter (see problem 1).

problems.title: On-medication weigh-in de-emphasis is unexamined: receipts omit weigh-ins for the cohort whose prescriber titrates on trend
problems.evidence: WeeklyReview.swift:335 — 'if weighs > 0, chapter != .onMedication' excludes weigh-in clauses from the on-med week story; no comment documents the rationale.
problems.detail: Defensible instinct (don't celebrate drug-driven scale drops), but on-med users still need a live trend: the rapid-loss tripwire depends on weigh-ins to fire, and the trend is the objective datum their prescriber uses. Reframe rather than omit — weigh receipts for on-med should carry the muscle/fuel frame ('trend feeds your care, not your grade'), or the silent omission quietly starves the cohort's own safety signal.

recommendations.title: Build THE POST-MEDICATION ARC: a real .postMedication chapter that arms the band from the day she stops
recommendations.detail: Add a fourth chapter routed from glp1Status 'past' (Chapter.derive, DayModel.swift), collecting one field: roughly when she stopped. Weeks 1–12 off drug: (1) appetite-return normalization in the SleepSignal forgiveness register — 'food noise getting louder is the medication leaving, not your discipline failing'; (2) arm the existing BandZone drift/reset machinery from her stop-date settle weight instead of gating it behind .keeping; (3) carry the on-med strength/protein blocks forward unchanged; (4) tighten weigh-cadence encouragement (the earliest-drift-signal copy already exists in 'pattern_week'). Every mechanic already ships — this is re-pointing, not building. It is also the emptiest competitive space in the category and the exact patient my clinic cannot support between visits.

recommendations.title: Shot-day anchor: one collected scheduling fact that lets the on-med day shape itself around the injection week
recommendations.detail: Ask on-med users one question ('which day is your shot day?' — a calendar fact, no brand names, no dosing advice; compliance-clean). Then: day-after softening (smaller-plates permission, 'rough-stomach days are the medication, not you'), fluids-first care lines on shot day ±1, PrescriptionEngineV2 demotes the day's ask on post-shot days, and DailyBriefEngine gains a nausea-normalizing brief variant. Add a passive low-fuel care line for on-med from existing plate exhaust: evening + logged day < ~800 kcal → 'small and often counts. protein when it settles' (never a target, mirrors the existing 16h care line). This is the difference between a plan that exists and a plan that knows her week.

recommendations.title: Make strength a required beat for the on-medication chapter and give it a receipt
recommendations.detail: In DayModel.isOptional, exempt .workout from the optional demotion when chapter == .onMedication on strength-block days (or promote 2 strength days/week to required rows with the check ring); add a 'strength kept · N of 2 this week' receipt to the signals band and the WeeklyReview week story. Copy already exists ('two short strength sessions protect muscle'). Protein-plus-resistance is the lean-mass prescription; the app currently ships half of it as required and half as 'if you feel like it'.

recommendations.title: Resolve the fast-row contradiction: receipt grammar, not completion grammar (founder decision required)
recommendations.detail: Keep the row and the founder's naming, but remove the ≥12h done-state and check ring (TodayView fastRowModel): render it as an auto-measured fact ('13h between plates · measured') in the same isAuto style as steps-before-goal. Soften the window sheet's 'stores less / improved insulin sensitivity' to trial-attributed phrasing ('in trials, earlier eating tracked with…'). Retain every existing clamp (14h praise saturation, 16h care line, GLP-1 exclusion, QuietHours gates) — they are correct. This closes the one surface where the app's shipped UI contradicts its own encoded safety law.

recommendations.title: Clinician-visit prep card: auto-assembled from data the app already holds
recommendations.detail: A monthly, shareable one-pager (same machinery as the lesson share card): 60-day EMA trend, weigh-in cadence, protein-days-met, strength-days, average overnight window, sleep pattern — titled 'for your next appointment'. Zero diagnosis, zero advice; it is her data, organized. For on-med and post-med users this converts the app from a coach into care infrastructure, and it is the exact seam a white-label clinic deployment plugs into (the clinic dashboard is this card, continuously). Wire the rapid-loss brief to point at it: 'worth showing your clinician'.

recommendations.title: Cohort-tune the tripwires: on-med rapid-loss variant + regain vigilance outside .keeping
recommendations.detail: RapidLossTripwire gains a chapter-aware message: on-med adds the strength pairing and the visit-prep pointer; keep the 1%/wk ceiling (correct as a care trigger even when drug-expected). Add the mirror: for post-GLP-1 (and any user with isRegainRisk 'cycling'), a sustained-upward EMA (≥ ~0.5 kg over 3 weeks) opens the existing 'steadying week' machinery with the same zero-alarm register — currently that response is unreachable outside maintenance mode. Both are pure additions to DailyBriefEngine's ladder using fields already computed.

recommendations.title: Restore gentle weigh receipts for on-med with a reframed clause
recommendations.detail: Change WeeklyReview.weekStory's on-med exclusion (line 335) to a cohort-framed clause ('trend checked twice — it feeds your care') and keep weigh-cadence encouragement alive in the on-med rotation, because the tripwire, the prescriber conversation, and the post-med band all starve without weigh-ins. Document the rationale in-code either way; today the omission reads as accidental.

one_transformative_move: Build the post-medication arc: route glp1Status "past" to its own chapter that arms the existing band-zone drift/reset machinery from her stop-date settle weight, normalizes returning appetite in the forgiveness register before she feels it ("the food noise coming back is the medication leaving, not you failing"), and carries the protein+strength blocks forward for 12 weeks — the app already owns every mechanic this needs (BandZone, SleepSignal-style reframing, WeekIntent blocks, the tripwire pattern) but points them all away from the one cohort whose physiology guarantees the crisis; being the app that was already watching for the regain window is both the strongest possible proof of "jeni is already paying attention" and the single feature that would make me consider white-labeling this for my own patients.
care_plan_ideas: Shot-day rhythm care: one collected shot-day field drives post-injection softening — smaller-plate permission, fluids-first lines, demoted asks on rough days, nausea normalized as chemistry (no brand names, no dosing talk)

The lean-mass pair as the on-med daily non-negotiables: protein floor + 2 weekly strength beats both required, with weekly kept-receipts (protein days ≥5, strength 2 of 2) — the two numbers a clinic MA would ask about at follow-up

Post-discontinuation 12-week plan: appetite-return normalization, band zones armed from stop-date settle weight, weekly trend check, 'the drug leaves, the habits stay' framing with a kind rapid-regain steadying week

A 1-tap daily state check (appetite loud/quiet · stomach rough/okay · energy low/fine) feeding a weekly burden trend — the PRO layer that flags rising side-effect burden to a clinician and softens the app's own asks

Passive low-fuel care line for on-med users from existing plate exhaust: logged day under ~800 kcal by evening → 'small and often counts, fluids first, protein when it settles' (care register, never a target)

Clinician-visit prep card auto-assembled monthly (EMA trend, weigh cadence, protein/strength days, window average, burden trend) — 'show this at your next appointment'; in white-label form this IS the clinic dashboard, with hard rules on what escalates to the physician (rapid loss/regain, chronic protein misses, SCOFF-positive emergence, burden rising 2+ weeks) and what is never automated (dose/titration/stop-start advice, symptom interpretation, ED handling beyond screen-and-route, crisis beyond warm human routing)
